source: research/part11 A5, D6: audit trail keeps old and new value; changes never obscure earlier data
artifact: Analysts correct a typed nitrosamine result by overwriting the value in the results table. An audit row stores the new value, the user ID and the server timestamp.

source: research/iso17025 7.10: impact on earlier results, customer notification and recall, authorised resumption
artifact: An out-of-tolerance balance verification opens a Deviation with a description and an owner. The balance is blocked until any Analyst closes the Deviation with a closing comment.

source: research/part11 B1-B3, C4-C5: signature shows name, time, meaning; bound to record; re-authenticates
artifact: Reviewer approval of a result is a checkbox on the review screen. Ticking it stores the reviewer's user ID and the time.

source: research/iso17025 7.7.3: failed batch QC must prevent incorrect results being reported
artifact: When a batch's spiked recovery or blank fails its acceptance criteria, the review screen shows a yellow warning banner. The Reviewer can still approve the batch and QA can release its reports.

source: research/iso17025 6.2.6: people are authorised, not just trained, to review and release
artifact: Review sign-off checks only that the Reviewer holds a current Training Record for the method. QA release checks only that the user has the QA role.

QA release is an e-signature. The signing dialog always asks for the password and a fresh TOTP code, even inside a session. The server stores an immutable signature row with printed name, username, role, UTC time plus the lab's zone, meaning 'Released', record ID, record version, and a SHA-256 hash of the canonical record content. Every screen and PDF of the record renders the signature block. Any later change creates a new record version, whose hash no longer matches, so it shows as unsigned until re-signed. Signature rows are audit-trailed.

Each equipment record holds: identity with software and firmware version; manufacturer, type and serial number; verification evidence; current location; calibration dates, results, adjustments, acceptance criteria and due date; reference-material documentation, results, acceptance criteria, dates and period of validity; maintenance plan and maintenance done; and any damage, malfunction, modification or repair.

source: calibration traceability is ISO/IEC 17025 6.5, not a Part 11 rule
artifact: Balance calibration certificates are uploaded as PDF files with a due date. The calibration provider's accreditation and the stated uncertainty are not recorded.

source: lockout and idle logout are Part 11 §11.300(d) / draft Annex 11 §11.7-11.8 rules
artifact: Login locks after 3 failed attempts and unlocks itself after 15 minutes. Each user can turn off the idle logout in their profile.

source: research/cn: every change to entered critical data must be approved (CS Art. 16)
artifact: For specifications under China jurisdiction, an Analyst corrects a typed result by creating a new result version with a mandatory reason. The audit trail keeps the old and new values, the user, the role and the UTC time. Nobody approves the correction.

source: research/jp: automatic pass/fail is advisory; QA records its own judgment (JIREI GMP20-11)
artifact: For Japanese customers, the LIMS computes pass or fail against the specification and that computed result is final. QA release signs the report without recording a judgment of its own.

source: research/eu: data and audit trail read-only after release (A11d §17.1)
artifact: For EU customers, after QA release a Lab Manager can still correct a typo in a released result by entering a reason. The audit trail records the change.
